questions.question: Which language should the desktop dashboard use?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Typed application code for Angular and Electron.

questions.question: Which frontend framework should power the desktop dashboard?

options.label: Angular (latest stable)
options.description: Use the latest stable Angular release with Angular Material.

questions.question: What should the desktop dashboard include?
questions.answer: Poll GET /api/dashboard every second. Show velocity, pressure, and temperature with animated circular gauges, current value and unit, status, and updated time. Display an individual live trend chart for each metric with zoom, pan, and tooltips; loading, connection, and error states; runtime unit conversion without a backend request; a live light/dark theme; and CSV and Excel export.
questions.recommendedChoice: Poll GET /api/dashboard every second. Show velocity, pressure, and temperature with animated circular gauges, current value and unit, status, and updated time. Display an individual live trend chart for each metric with zoom, pan, and tooltips; loading, connection, and error states; runtime unit conversion without a backend request; a live light/dark theme; and CSV and Excel export.

questions.question: Which backend framework should provide the local telemetry API?
questions.answer: Node.js with Express, started and stopped by Electron

options.label: Node.js with Express, started and stopped by Electron
options.description: A small localhost-only API for a reliable desktop demo.

questions.recommendedChoice: Node.js with Express, started and stopped by Electron

questions.question: What should the local telemetry API do?
questions.answer: Implement GET /api/dashboard and generate velocity, pressure, and temperature telemetry in memory every second. Apply approximately +/-10% random changes and every fifth cycle gradually drift toward baseline. Keep and return only the latest 100 samples. Bind to localhost and let Electron manage the API lifecycle.
questions.recommendedChoice: Implement GET /api/dashboard and generate velocity, pressure, and temperature telemetry in memory every second. Apply approximately +/-10% random changes and every fifth cycle gradually drift toward baseline. Keep and return only the latest 100 samples. Bind to localhost and let Electron manage the API lifecycle.
